a1-rescue-sec.heading: My Acute Rescue Remedies (the section's opening, before its list of remedies)
a1-rescue-sec.for: a reader learns what the list of rescue remedies that follows is for: acute trouble where the body, the gut or the brain is what is going wrong, as against a mainly emotional crisis. The first five paragraphs are the writer's own or already settled and stay. Read the last two paragraphs (from "If a trip comes with diarrhea"). In them, that first sentence, "Those trips are what the remedies below are for ..." and the last line are settled; the new sentences are the three after the first (what loss of bodily control and neurological disorganization look like, and calling medics) and the two about mental hell and gut hell
a1-rescue-sec.moment: you are sitting with a friend on a psychedelic who has diarrhea and nausea and says their mind is going crazy; you are deciding whether this is something to talk them through or something to treat with a remedy

a1-gut-sec.heading: Gut-Toxin & Die-Off Tools (the section's opening, before its first remedy, ZeoCharge & Ferment, a zeolite powder in water and a fermented juice)
a1-gut-sec.for: a reader learns why the gut remedies come first and what to make of nausea and diarrhea on a psychedelic. The first paragraph stands in the guide already; read the two new paragraphs after it
a1-gut-sec.moment: you are about to take a psychedelic, or to sit with a friend who has, and you are deciding whether to have a gut remedy ready and what to do when the nausea or diarrhea comes
